title: Change Assurance Decision Catalog for Model Traffic Orchestration
creator: Asha Patel
description: Objective: Define a compact, machine-readable catalog of change-assurance gates and sign-off templates that govern canary rollouts, A/B experiments, shadow traffic paths, and auto-rollback triggers for model promotions. Scope includes RBAC roles for approval, required evidence bundles (metrics + sample outputs), audit-log schema for forensic review, timeboxed escalation rules, and automated enforcement hooks that integrate with runtime routing and the Console. Out of scope: model evaluation heuristics (covered by Eval team) and per-customer legal approval workflows.
acceptance_criteria: 1) RBAC templates defined for three roles (Requester, Reviewer, Approver) with required entitlement checks documented; 2) Sign-off templates created for canary, shadow, and A/B flows with required evidence fields; 3) Audit-log JSON schema and retention policy drafted and agreed with Security; 4) Auto-rollback triggers (SLO breach and anomaly detection) defined and mapped to rollback playbooks; 5) Minimal PoC implemented to attach a sign-off bundle to a canary promotion API call and record audit events to the audit sink.
proposed_design_summary:
- Decision catalog: a YAML/JSON schema that enumerates gate types (manual-approval, timebox, metric-threshold, anomaly-detect), signers required, minimum sample size, and escalation path.
- RBAC: map Linear roles to product entitlements; integrate with SSO groups and Dedicated role-mappings.
- Audit bundle: evidence set includes dashboard snapshot links, token-level cost delta, per-route latency percentiles, human-reviewed failure samples, and PR/Confluence links.
- Enforcement: Console validates required approvals at promotion time; API returns 412 if missing. Autonomy agents (rollout-controller) listen to approval events to advance stage or trigger rollback.
tradeoffs_and_notes: Prefer compact, machine-validated sign-off bundles rather than free-text approvals to enable automation, but require human-readable context for auditors.
Tight coupling of approval checks to runtime increases safety but adds latency to promotion; mitigate via preflight checks and cached attestations.
Retention window for audit logs affects cost; propose 1 year hot + 4 years cold storage as baseline for enterprise customers.
We will avoid embedding eval logic in the catalog; instead reference external eval artifact IDs to keep the catalog lightweight.
security_considerations: Audit logs must include actor, actor_ip, action, target_model_version, prior_state, evidence_refs. Logs are write-once and signed; KMS-backed signing required for enterprise. RBAC template changes themselves must be reviewable and require multi-sig for high-privilege roles.
tests_and_poC_plan: 1) Create a test canary promotion that requires a Review sign-off and attach a synthetic evidence bundle. 2) Confirm Console blocks promotion when bundle is missing. 3) Simulate an SLO breach via loadtest and verify rollback-controller triggers rollback and writes audit entry. 4) Run a legal audit read of stored bundles for completeness.
implementation_steps: 1) Draft decision catalog schema + examples (this ticket). 2) API schema changes for promotion endpoints (ENG). 3) Console UX for sign-off flow (DES). 4) Rollout-controller hook to read approvals and enforce auto-rollback (ENG). 5) Security sign-off and KMS integration (SEC). 6) PoC and smoke tests, then ship to the staging org.
updates: 2025-02-12 — Asha Patel: Ticket created after leadership review. Initial scope and acceptance criteria added.
2025-02-18 — Liam Chen: Reached out to ENG owners (ENG-4210) to align API contract. Agreed to add promotion endpoint flag 'approval_bundle'.
2025-02-25 — Design review (Marta Ruiz): Console wireframes for sign-off modal posted to Drive; requested an optional 'annotated sample output' field in evidence bundle.
2025-02-28 — Security (Noah Singh): Reviewed audit schema; asked for KMS signing for enterprise and retention options. Marked security_review_required=true.
2025-03-03 — Product: Decided to treat A/B experiments with <10% traffic differently: allow 'expedited' sign-off (single approver) with stricter post-rollout monitoring.
review_feedback: ENG: prefer stateless evidence refs (artifact IDs) rather than embedding large snapshots; Console can render snapshots by dereferencing IDs.
Design: keep sign-off modal <5 fields on first pass; advanced evidence can be attached from the bundle explorer.
Security: require immutable audit artifact signing for any 'approve' action in dedicated/private deployments.
open_risks: Approval fatigue if too many rollouts require full committee sign-off; mitigated by tiering and delegated approvals.
Misconfigured auto-rollback thresholds could cause noisy rollbacks during transient infra issues; need clear SLO calibration and hysteresis.
next_steps: Finalize decision catalog schema and publish examples (owner: PM).
ENG to propose promotion API patch and retention storage plan (owner: ENG).
DES to prepare sign-off modal copy and accessibility review (owner: DES).

notes: Avoid naming collisions with existing 'approval' docs by focusing on a machine-readable decision catalog rather than governance policy prose.
